title: Choose what must survive a restart
summary: Redis persistence settings decide how data is written to disk.
introduction: Redis persistence settings decide how data is written to disk. Your task: Classify a temporary reading-tip key as replaceable or essential.
learningObjectives: Classify a temporary reading-tip key as replaceable or essential.
Explain the example for choose what must survive a restart

blocks.text: Redis persistence settings decide how data is written to disk. A cache may be rebuildable, while important records need a deliberate durability plan.
Use a local Redis server and redis-cli. Commands here use cma: practice keys only. Redis commands do not run in the site's SQLite playground. Do not connect these exercises to a production database.

blocks.code:
Example decision:
Cached book summary: can be loaded again if lost.
Only copy of a payment record: must not depend on an unreviewed cache setup.
Check the server's RDB snapshot and AOF settings, then test a practice restart.
blocks.title: Choose what must survive a restart

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: A cached copy can be rebuilt from another trusted source.
The only copy of an important record needs a reviewed persistence and restore plan, not an assumed cache guarantee.

blocks.text: The worked decision separates replaceable cache data from records that need stronger guarantees.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Do not assume in-memory speed means guaranteed persistence. Backups and restore tests are separate jobs.
